title: PASSIVE VOICE
notes:
✓ Passive voice → a sentence structure in which the receiver of an action becomes the main focus.

✓ Active → The teacher explained the lesson.
✓ Passive → The lesson was explained by the teacher.

✓ Active voice focuses on the DOER.
✓ Passive voice focuses on the ACTION or RECEIVER.

✓ Basic structure → subject + be + past participle (V3) + (by + agent).

title: ACTIVE VS PASSIVE
notes:
✓ Active voice → subject + verb + object.
✓ The students cleaned the classroom.

✓ Passive voice → object + be + V3 + by + subject.
✓ The classroom was cleaned by the students.

✓ Transformation:
The students → the agent.
cleaned → action.
the classroom → receiver.

→ Passive → The classroom was cleaned by the students.

title: BASIC RULE
notes:
✓ To form the passive, use the appropriate form of BE + past participle (V3).

✓ Active → subject + verb + object.
✓ Passive → object + BE + V3 + (by + agent).

✓ write → written
✓ build → built
✓ make → made
✓ take → taken

✓ The tense is shown by the form of BE, while the main verb becomes V3.

title: PRESENT SIMPLE PASSIVE
notes:
✓ Structure → am/is/are + V3.

✓ Active → People speak English worldwide.
✓ Passive → English is spoken worldwide.

✓ Active → Workers produce cars here.
✓ Passive → Cars are produced here.

✓ am → I
✓ is → singular noun
✓ are → plural noun.

title: PAST SIMPLE PASSIVE
notes:
✓ Structure → was/were + V3.

✓ Active → They built the bridge in 2010.
✓ Passive → The bridge was built in 2010.

✓ Active → They cleaned the rooms.
✓ Passive → The rooms were cleaned.

✓ was → singular.
✓ were → plural.

title: FUTURE SIMPLE PASSIVE
notes:
✓ Structure → will be + V3.

✓ Active → They will finish the project tomorrow.
✓ Passive → The project will be finished tomorrow.

✓ Active → They will announce the results soon.
✓ Passive → The results will be announced soon.

✓ Future passive → will + be + past participle.

title: PRESENT CONTINUOUS PASSIVE
notes:
✓ Structure → am/is/are + being + V3.

✓ Active → They are repairing the road.
✓ Passive → The road is being repaired.

✓ Active → Workers are building the house.
✓ Passive → The house is being built.

✓ Continuous passive requires BE + BEING + V3.

title: PAST CONTINUOUS PASSIVE
notes:
✓ Structure → was/were + being + V3.

✓ Active → They were repairing the road.
✓ Passive → The road was being repaired.

✓ Active → Workers were painting the walls.
✓ Passive → The walls were being painted.

✓ Past continuous passive → was/were + being + V3.

title: PRESENT PERFECT PASSIVE
notes:
✓ Structure → has/have + been + V3.

✓ Active → They have completed the work.
✓ Passive → The work has been completed.

✓ Active → They have cleaned the rooms.
✓ Passive → The rooms have been cleaned.

✓ Perfect passive → have/has + been + V3.

title: PAST PERFECT PASSIVE
notes:
✓ Structure → had + been + V3.

✓ Active → They had finished the work.
✓ Passive → The work had been finished.

✓ Active → Someone had stolen the car.
✓ Passive → The car had been stolen.

✓ Past perfect passive → had + been + V3.

title: FUTURE PERFECT PASSIVE
notes:
✓ Structure → will have been + V3.

✓ Active → They will have completed the project by Friday.
✓ Passive → The project will have been completed by Friday.

✓ Future perfect passive → will + have + been + V3.

title: PASSIVE TENSE SUMMARY
notes:
✓ Present simple → am/is/are + V3
Example → The room is cleaned.

✓ Past simple → was/were + V3
Example → The room was cleaned.

✓ Future simple → will be + V3
Example → The room will be cleaned.

✓ Present continuous → am/is/are being + V3
Example → The room is being cleaned.

✓ Past continuous → was/were being + V3
Example → The room was being cleaned.

✓ Present perfect → has/have been + V3
Example → The room has been cleaned.

✓ Past perfect → had been + V3
Example → The room had been cleaned.

✓ Future perfect → will have been + V3
Example → The room will have been cleaned.

title: PASSIVE WITH MODAL VERBS
notes:
✓ Modal + be + V3.

✓ Active → You must obey the rules.
✓ Passive → The rules must be obeyed.

✓ Active → They can solve the problem.
✓ Passive → The problem can be solved.

✓ Active → We should protect the environment.
✓ Passive → The environment should be protected.

✓ Common modals → can, could, may, might, must, should, would.

✓ Structure → modal + be + V3.

title: HAVE TO & NEED TO IN PASSIVE
notes:
✓ Have to → have/has to be + V3.

✓ Active → Students have to complete the assignment.
✓ Passive → The assignment has to be completed.

✓ Need to → need to be + V3.
✓ Active → We need to repair the road.
✓ Passive → The road needs to be repaired.

✓ The passive keeps the obligation/necessity while changing the focus to the receiver.

title: THE 'BY' PHRASE
notes:
✓ The person or thing that performs the action can be introduced with by.

✓ The novel was written by the author.
✓ The bridge was built by engineers.

✓ Use 'by + agent' when the doer is important, new, or necessary to the meaning.

✓ Omit the agent when it is unknown, obvious, unimportant, or general.

✓ My phone was stolen.
→ We do not know who stole it.

✓ English is spoken here.
→ The speakers are not important.

title: WHEN TO USE PASSIVE
notes:
✓ Passive voice is useful when:

◆ 1. The receiver of the action is more important.
✓ The bridge was opened yesterday.

◆ 2. The agent is unknown.
✓ My bicycle was stolen.

◆ 3. The agent is obvious.
✓ He was arrested.

◆ 4. The agent is unimportant.
✓ The road is being repaired.

◆ 5. Formal or scientific writing focuses on processes and results.
✓ The solution was heated to 80°C.

✓ Passive voice is common in news reports, academic writing, scientific descriptions, and formal communication.

title: PASSIVE QUESTIONS
notes:
✓ Questions keep the auxiliary verb before the subject.

✓ Active → Did they build the house?
✓ Passive → Was the house built?

✓ Active → Are they repairing the road?
✓ Passive → Is the road being repaired?

✓ Active → Have they finished the work?
✓ Passive → Has the work been finished?

✓ Active → Will they announce the results?
✓ Passive → Will the results be announced?

title: PASSIVE NEGATIVES
notes:
✓ Put 'not' after the auxiliary verb.

✓ The work is not finished.
✓ The car was not repaired.
✓ The results have not been announced.
✓ The project will not be completed today.
✓ The rules must not be broken.

✓ The position of 'not' depends on the auxiliary structure.

title: TWO OBJECTS IN THE PASSIVE
notes:
✓ Some verbs can have two objects, allowing two passive structures.

✓ Active → She gave me a book.

✓ Passive 1 → I was given a book.
✓ Passive 2 → A book was given to me.

✓ Active → They told him the truth.
✓ Passive → He was told the truth.

✓ Common verbs → give, send, offer, show, tell, lend, teach, promise.

title: VERBS WITH PREPOSITIONS
notes:
✓ In passive sentences, the preposition can remain after the verb.

✓ Active → Someone has looked after the child.
✓ Passive → The child has been looked after.

✓ Active → They laughed at him.
✓ Passive → He was laughed at.

✓ Do not remove the necessary preposition.

❌ He was laughed.
✓ He was laughed at.

title: GET-PASSIVE
notes:
✓ Get + past participle can form a more informal passive construction.

✓ He got injured in the accident.
✓ She got promoted last year.
✓ They got married in June.

✓ Get-passive is common in informal English and often emphasizes a change, event, or experience.

⚠️ For formal writing, the standard BE passive is generally preferred.

✓ He was injured in the accident.

title: PASSIVE WITH INFINITIVES
notes:
✓ Passive infinitive → to be + V3.

✓ Active → They expect him to finish the work.
✓ Passive → He is expected to finish the work.

✓ Active → People believe that he is honest.
✓ Passive → He is believed to be honest.

✓ Structure → to be + past participle when the infinitive itself is passive.

✓ The work needs to be completed.

title: PASSIVE GERUND
notes:
✓ Passive gerund → being + V3.

✓ He dislikes being criticized.
✓ She hates being ignored.
✓ I remember being invited to the event.

✓ Structure → being + past participle.

✓ Perfect passive gerund → having been + V3.
✓ He apologized for having been treated unfairly.

title: REPORTING PASSIVE
notes:
✓ Reporting verbs can be used in passive structures, especially in formal English.

✓ People say that he is rich.
→ It is said that he is rich.
→ He is said to be rich.

✓ People believe that she won the competition.
→ It is believed that she won the competition.
→ She is believed to have won the competition.

✓ Common reporting verbs → say, believe, think, know, expect, report, consider.

title: COMMON ERRORS
notes:
❌ The house built yesterday.
✓ The house was built yesterday.

❌ The letter was wrote.
✓ The letter was written.

❌ The work is finish.
✓ The work is finished.

❌ The road is being repair.
✓ The road is being repaired.

❌ The project has been complete.
✓ The project has been completed.

❌ The rules must followed.
✓ The rules must be followed.

❌ The car was repaired by him yesterday? → possible but awkward if 'by him' is unnecessary.
✓ The car was repaired yesterday.

✓ Always check: correct BE form + V3.

title: EXAM GUIDE
notes:
◆ 1. Find the OBJECT of the active sentence.

◆ 2. Move the object to the subject position.

◆ 3. Identify the tense of the active verb.

◆ 4. Use the correct form of BE for that tense.

◆ 5. Change the main verb to V3.

◆ 6. Add 'by + agent' only when necessary.

◆ QUICK FORMULAS
✓ Present simple → am/is/are + V3
✓ Past simple → was/were + V3
✓ Future → will be + V3
✓ Present continuous → am/is/are being + V3
✓ Past continuous → was/were being + V3
✓ Present perfect → has/have been + V3
✓ Past perfect → had been + V3
✓ Future perfect → will have been + V3
✓ Modal → modal + be + V3

✓ Golden rule → PASSIVE = appropriate form of BE + V3.

◆ EXAMPLE
✓ Active → Workers are building the bridge.
✓ Passive → The bridge is being built.

✓ Focus on the tense of 'BE', not the tense of the V3.
